title: field-echoes-sprint-notes-and-request-microledger-2028-03-14
content:
One-line summary:
A compact ‘microledger’ of customer feedback captured during Feb–Mar 2028 field calls and support threads; tiny fixes and short experiments (<=2w) that unblock customers or reduce repeated operational friction. This doc is meant for quick triage and sprint ingestion — each entry has a proposed lean patch, impact estimate, and next action.

Context and how this was compiled:
- Sources: 18 support threads, 6 enterprise calls (dedicated/private), three SRE incident follow-ups, and survey snippets from Feb 2028.
- Method: we parsed request verbs (block, confused, slow, inconsistent), clustered by immediate remediation vs. design-level work, and kept items that are implementable as micro-patches or small product experiments.
- Goal: reduce repetitive CS handoffs and lower TTR for top 10% of recurring asks.

Signal highlights (high-level themes):
- "Routing opacity": customers frequently confused by how requests fall back to model variants when capacity is constrained. Typical phrasing: "why did my request suddenly use a cheaper model?"
- "Token billing surprises": customers report unclear multipliers when function/tool calling or streaming triggers extra tokens.
- "Private deployment sanity checks": small misconfigurations during VPC onboarding cause confusing errors that are hard to debug without a single-line failure cause.
- "Embeddings mismatch": occasional drift in returned embedding sizes or metadata fields when model defaults change during a catalog refresh.
- "Console latency spikes": customers see variable percentiles in Console charts compared to raw API traces.

Prioritized microledger (ranked by frequency * fix-effort):
1) Patch: "Fallback hint in response headers"
   - Customer quote: "We had three incidents where our app fell back to a lower-tier model and the UI showed odd completions; we couldn't tell why."
   - Frequency: frequent (reported by 6 customers last 30d)
   - Impact: High (developer trust, debugging time)
   - Proposal: Add an optional debug header (X-Redwood-Model-Fallback: original=<model>, active=<model>, reason=<policy>) for requests when routing substitutes model variants. Default off for prod; opt-in via header or account setting.
   - Owner: eng-platform (tbd) / SE for quick docs blurb
   - Risk: low; read-only metadata
   - Dev estimate: 2–3d + 1d docs
   - Next action: PR draft + doc snippet (owner: Priya)

2) Patch: "Token-call delta preview in Console"
   - Customer quote: "Our finance team saw a 40% jump month-over-month after enabling tool-calls; we couldn't reconcile charges."
   - Frequency: medium
   - Impact: High (billing surprises hurt trust and enterprise renewals)
   - Proposal: Console quick-view per route: shows estimated tokens for the last 7 days with a toggle that simulates enabling tool-calls/streaming to show delta.
   - Owner: product-console + billing
   - Risk: medium (estimation complexity)
   - Dev estimate: 1 sprint for a lightweight MVP (backend estimate + UI mock)
   - Next action: design wireframe and backend sample query (owner: Liam)

3) Patch: "VPC onboarding sanity-checker script (diagnostic)"
   - Customer quote: "We kept getting 'timeout' during handshake — support said subnet route table mismatch; we didn't know where to look."
   - Frequency: recurrent for new private customers
   - Impact: Medium-high (reduces CS time-to-resolution)
   - Proposal: Small Python CLI that runs a checklist against customer's VPC settings (DNS, route table, security groups, egress rules) and produces a single-line summary + suggested fix. Ship as part of Private onboarding docs and as a runnable support tool.
   - Owner: private-deployments + SEs
   - Risk: low (non-invasive checks)
   - Dev estimate: 3–5d for initial checks
   - Next action: compile canonical checklist (owner: Diego)

4) Patch: "Embedding schema guard"
   - Customer quote: "After your model catalog update, our DB ingestion pipeline tripped on a changed embedding length."
   - Frequency: low but high impact when it happens
   - Impact: High for downstream ingestion reliability
   - Proposal: When model catalog changes default embedding size or field schema, add a short deprecation notice and a compatibility-mode header that keeps prior behavior for N days. Also add a Console alert for admins.
   - Owner: product-hosted-api + applied-ml
   - Risk: medium (catalog semantics)
   - Dev estimate: 1 sprint for alerting + 2d for header
   - Next action: runbook for catalog changes (owner: Priya)

5) Patch: "Console vs. API trace alignment"
   - Customer quote: "Your Console p95 is showing 120ms but our traces show 350ms for the same token events."
   - Frequency: medium
   - Impact: Medium (confusion; false SLO alarms)
   - Proposal: Add a small note in Console explaining measurement windows and an optional raw-trace overlay to compare Console percentiles against exported raw traces.
   - Owner: observability
   - Risk: low
   - Dev estimate: 3–5d for overlay MVP
   - Next action: prototype trace overlay (owner: Priya)

Quick wins (<=1d) (can be slotted into next-standup):
- Update hosted API docs to call out token behavior when streaming vs. buffered responses are used (owner: docs team).
- Add snippet to onboarding checklist that highlights common misconfig for Private customers (owner: SE).
- Make a CS canned response template that explains model-fallback behavior & where to find fallback headers for opt-in debugging (owner: Maya).

Cross-cutting observations (patterns across requests):
- Many asks are about observability & transparency rather than new features. Customers prefer more data to self-diagnose than product changes.
- Small UI changes (headers, Console toggles, diagnostic scripts) are disproportionately effective to restore trust.
- A handful of customers are sensitive to catalog changes; better advance notice and compatibility options reduce churn risk.

Open questions / trade-offs we need to decide quickly:
- Should fallback metadata be visible by default for higher-tier accounts? Pros: faster debugging; Cons: leak routing policies.
- What is acceptable estimation variance for token-delta simulator in Console? (accuracy vs. speed of compute)
- For embedding schema changes, do we prefer a header compatibility window or a true versioned API? (short term header seems easier)

Stakeholder asks and suggested owners (tiny roadmap sketch):
- CS: canned responses + micro-FAQ for model fallbacks (owner: Maya) — target 2028-03-28
- Eng-platform: fallback header PR + opt-in flag (owner: eng-platform lead) — target 2028-04-04
- Console: token-delta view prototype (owner: product-console) — target 2028-04-11
- Private: VPC sanity CLI + docs (owner: private-deployments) — target 2028-04-04

Meeting notes (field calls 3/12–3/13):
- Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Diego, SE rep from XCorp
- XCorp: hardest pain is billing surprises from async agent tests. They requested a monthly token-breakdown CSV export per route.
- YBank: requested an 'audit mode' for Private where errors are verbose for first 24h of onboarding only.
- ZStartup: asked for a tiny SDK snippet to detect model fallback and log it locally. We suggested using the debug header (if available).

Next steps (concrete):
1) Draft the CS canned responses and internal playbook (owner: Maya) — due 2028-03-18
2) Priya to create two mock console screens (token-delta + raw-trace overlay) and attach to this doc — due 2028-03-20
3) Diego to assemble VPC checklist + PoC CLI; share in #private-onboarding — due 2028-03-21
4) Liam to open a lightweight platform ticket for fallback header + small RFC for safelisting behavior (due 2028-03-19)

Appendix: short raw snippets (redacted)
- "We saw the model swap mid-stream and completions got shorter — our users noticed and downgraded." — Customer A
- "Billing went up after we enabled tool-calls; we didn't have any way to quantify the change quickly." — Customer B

Notes-to-self: keep microledger small and shipable. If it grows past 12 items, split into 'micro' and 'patchback' lanes.
